AESDECRYPT.summary: AESDECRYPT () decrypts a text string that was encrypted using the AESENCRYPT() function.

params.name: aeskeyid
params.description: An integer value in the range of one to five. It must match the value that was used to encrypt the string using AESENCRYPT().

params.name: customkey
params.description: A 16-character string to use for the decryption. It must match the value that was used to encrypt the string using AESENCRYPT().

params.name: inbuf
params.description: The encrypted string that was created using the AESENCRYPT() function.

params.name: inbuflen
params.description: An integer value that represents the length of the character string to be decrypted.

params.name: mode
params.description: An integer value limited to 0 (for base-10) or 1 (for base-16)

AESDECRYPT.example:
SET ENCRYPT_VAR = AESENCRYPT(1,"ABC12345xyz",TEXTLEN("ABC12345XYZ"),0)
SET DECRYPT_VAR = AESDECRYPT(1, ENCRYPT_VAR,TEXTLEN(ENCRYPT_VAR),0)

AESDECRYPTFILE.summary: The AESDECRYPTFILE( ) function decrypts a file that was encrypted using AESENCRYPTFILE().

params.name: Aeskeyid
params.description: Integer value in the range of 1 - 5, must match the value that was used when the file was encrypted using AESENCRYPTFILE()

params.name: Infile
params.description: Name of encrypted file

params.name: Outfile
params.description: Name of decrypted file to create

params.name: Password
params.description: Nonblank password or blank password. If a nonblank password was used when the file was encrypted using AESENCRYPTFILE(), the same nonblank password must be used to decrypt the file using AESDECRYPTFILE().

params.name: Mode
params.description: Integer value - Limited to 0 (for base 10) or 1 (for base 16)

AESDECRYPTFILE.example:
SELECT INTO CCL_TEST
	P.PERSON_ID,
	NAME = SUBSTRING(1,40,P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED)
FROM PERSON P
WITH FORMAT, MAXREC = 10

SET STAT = AESENCRYPTFILE(1,"CCL_TEST.DAT","CCL_ENCRYPT.DAT","PWD",0)
SET STAT = AESDECRYPTFILE(1,"CCL_ENCRYPT.DAT","CCL_DECRYPT.DAT","PWD",0)

params.name: customkey

params.name: inbuf

params.name: inbuflen

params.name: mode
params.description: Integer value - limited to 0 (for base-10) or 1 (for base-16).

AESENCRYPTFILE.summary: The AESENCRYPTFILE( ) function allows you to create an encrypted file using Advanced Encryption Standard (AES). The AESDECRYPTFILE() function can be used to decrypt a file that was encrypted using AESENCRYPTFILE().

params.name: aeskeyid

params.name: infile

params.name: outfile

params.name: password

params.name: mode

SET STAT = AESDECRYPTFILE(1,"CCL_ENCRYPT.DAT","CCL_DECRYPT.DAT","PWD",0)

ALTER.syntax:
ALTER(record_structure_list_item, dimension)
CALL ALTER(record_structure_list_item, dimension)  ;return type is discarded when using CALL
ALTER.summary: The ALTER( ) function allocates a contiguous block of memory to store information in a record structure list_item that was defined in the RECORD command using an integer value inside the [] square brackets. It Returns 1 if successful, 0 if not successful.

params.name: record_structure_list_item
params.description: A record structure list_item that was defined in the RECORD command using an integer value inside the [] square brackets.

params.name: dimension
params.description: A number representing the total number of positions to define in the record structure list_item. Before Discern Explorer version 8.12.3.1, an integer data type was required for the dimension.

ALTER.example:
; ...
         /*if all available positions of the QUAL list have been used, add 10 more */
         IF (MOD(COUNT,10) = 1 AND COUNT > 10 )
              STAT = ALTER(REC1->QUAL,COUNT + 9)
         ENDIF
	REC1->QUAL[COUNT]->FLD1 = P.NAME_LAST_KEY

FOOT REPORT
         /*resize the QUAL list down to the number of positions that were used */
	STAT = ALTER(REC1->QUAL,COUNT)

END
GO

ALTER2.syntax:
ALTER2(record_structure_list_item, dimension)
CALL ALTER2(record_structure_list_item, dimension)  ;return type is discarded when using CALL
ALTER2.summary: The ALTER2( ) function determines if the record structure list item is a contiguous record structure segment or a varlist record structure segment then calls the ALTER() or ALTERLIST() function accordingly. Returns 1 if successful, and 0 if not successful. The ALTER2() function was introduced in version 8.6.3 of Discern Explorer . The option to use CALL ALTER2( ) was introduced in version 8.9.2 of Discern Explorer .

params.name: record_structure_list_item
params.description: A record structure list_item that was defined using the RECORD command.

params.name: dimension
params.description: An integer representing the total number of positions to define in the record structure list_item.

ALTER2.example:
; ...
	COUNT = 0
	/* allocate 10 positions in the rec2->qual list*/
	STAT = ALTER2(REC2->QUAL,10)

DETAIL
	COUNT = COUNT + 1
	/*if all available positions of the QUAL lists have been used, add 10 more */
	IF (MOD(COUNT,10) = 1 AND COUNT > 1 )
		STAT = ALTER2(REC1->QUAL,COUNT + 9)
		STAT = ALTER2(REC2->QUAL,COUNT + 9)
	ENDIF
	REC1->QUAL[COUNT]->NAME = P.NAME_LAST_KEY
; ...

ALTER3.syntax:
ALTER3(record_structure_list_item, dimension)
CALL ALTER3(record_structure_list_item, dimension)  ;return type is discarded when using CALL
ALTER3.summary: The ALTER3( ) function determines if the record structure list item is a contiguous record structure segment or a varlist record structure segment. It then calls the ALTER() or ALTERLIST() function accordingly to increase the size of the record structure segment. ALTER3 only increases the size of the record structure segment. It does not decrease the size. It returns 1 if successful, or 0 if not successful.

params.name: record_structure_list_item
params.description: A record structure list_item that was defined using the RECORD command.

params.name: dimension
params.description: An integer representing the total number of positions to define in the record structure list_item.

ALTER3.example:
; ...
	COUNT = 0
	/* allocate 10 positions in the rec2->qual list*/
	STAT = ALTER3(REC2->QUAL,10)

DETAIL
	COUNT = COUNT + 1
	/*if all available positions of the QUAL lists have been used, add 10 more */
	IF (MOD(COUNT,10) = 1 AND COUNT > 1 )
		STAT = ALTER3(REC1->QUAL,COUNT + 9)
		STAT = ALTER3(REC2->QUAL,COUNT + 9)
	ENDIF
	REC1->QUAL[COUNT]->NAME = P.NAME_LAST_KEY
; ...

ALTERLIST.syntax:
ALTERLIST(record_structure_list_item, dimension [,insert_dimension])
CALL ALTERLIST(record_structure_list_item, dimension [,insert_dimension])  ;return type is discarded when using CALL
ALTERLIST.summary: The ALTERLIST( ) function allocates a block of memory in a linked list to store information in a record structure list_item that was defined in the RECORD command using an asterisk (*) inside the [] square brackets. Returns 1 if successful, 0 if not successful. When a RECORD command that defines a list_item using an asterisk (*) inside the square brackets [] is executed, no memory is allocated to store the positions of the list.

params.name: record_structure_list_item
params.description: A record structure list_item that was defined in the RECORD command using an asterisk * inside the [] square brackets.

params.name: dimension
params.description: A number representing the total number of positions to define in the record structure list_item. Before Discern Explorer version 8.12.3.1, an integer data type was required for the dimension.

params.name: insert_dimension
params.description: An integer representing a position of the current list. Positions will be added or removed from the list after the insert_dimension. If the parameter is omitted, the default is to add or remove the positions at the end.

ALTERLIST.example:
; ...
HEAD REPORT
	/* initialize 100 positions in the QUAL list_item */
	call alterlist(REC1->QUAL,100)
	/* create counter variable to keep track of the number of positions in the QUAL list_item */
	PCOUNT1 = 0

DETAIL
	PCOUNT1 = PCOUNT1 + 1
	/* if needed add 10 positions on the QUAL list_item */
	IF (MOD(PCOUNT1,10) = 1 AND PCOUNT1 > 100)
		call alterlist(REC1->QUAL,PCOUNT1 + 9)
	ENDIF
; ...

ARRAYJOIN.summary: The ARRAYJOIN() function joins the fields in a Record list into a character data type variable. The function returns the result by recursively joining the fields into a single output variable. The ARRAYJOIN() function was introduced in Discern Explorer version 8.12.3 and enhanced in Discern Explorer version 8.12.5.

params.name: record_structure_list
params.description: A Record Structure list name

params.name: field_separator
params.description: The characters used to separate the fields in the Record Structure list

params.name: list_separator
params.description: The characters used to separate the positions of the Record Structure list

params.name: delimiter
params.description: A character used to surround the values from the fields in the Record Structure list. By default, the delimiter is only applied to character fields

params.name: option_bits
params.description: An integer value representing the bitwise BOR (the bit_number to bit_number OR comparison) on the table below

ARRAYJOIN.table:
| Integer | Bit Option | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | BIT0 | Delimits all items using the delimiter |
| 2 | BIT1 | Formats dates to International Organization for Standardization (ISO) format |
| 4 | BIT2 | Formats dates to local format |
| 8 | BIT3 | Applies a field_separator between every field and not just the fields from a list; requires Discern... |
ARRAYJOIN.example:
; ...
      set myrec->list[cnt1].f6=fillstring(value(cnt1*10),char(cnt1+64))
  endfor
  Set jvar = ArrayJoin( myrec->list," and "," or ",'|')
  call echo(concat("jvar= ",jvar))
  Set jvar = ArrayJoin( myrec->list," and "," or ",'|',1)
  call echo(concat("option bit 1, jvar= ",jvar))
  Set jvar = ArrayJoin( myrec->list," and "," or ",'|',2)
  call echo(concat("option bit 2, jvar= ",jvar))
  Set jvar = ArrayJoin( myrec->list," and "," or ",'|',3)
  call echo(concat("option bit 3, jvar= ",jvar))
  Set jvar = ArrayJoin( myrec->list," and "," or ",'|',4)
  call echo(concat("option bit 4, jvar= ",jvar))
; ...

ARRAYSPLIT.summary: The ARRAYSPLIT() function iterates through a delimited string, extracts the delimited values, and inserts them into a record structure list item. This function was introduced in Discern Explorer versions 8.13.0 and 9.01.0. The original release returned the number of delimited values minus 1. Discern Explorer versions 8.13.2, 9.01.02, and higher return the number of delimited pieces.

params.name: record_item
params.description: A reference to a record structure list item that must be defined before the ARRAYSPLIT() function is called.

params.name: index_variable
params.description: An integer data type variable that must be declared before the ARRAYSPLIT() function is called. The index_variable is used as the subscript for the list in the record_item.

params.name: string _expression
params.description: A delimited character string.

params.name: delimiter
params.description: The delimiter is the character that delimits the string_expression value.

params.name: mode
params.description: Allows removal of leading blanks between quoted pieces, and embedding the delimiter in a quoted piece. The mode option was introduced in Discern Explorer versions 8.13.2 and 9.01.2.

ARRAYSPLIT.table:
| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Does not remove surrounding quotes from a piece, and retains lead blanks from a non-quote piece... |
| 1 | Removes surrounding quotes from a piece, and retains lead blanks from a non-quote piece. |
| 2 | Does not remove surrounding quotes from a piece, and removes lead blanks from a non-quote piece. |
| 3 | Removes surrounding quotes from a piece and lead blanks from a non-quote piece. |
| 4 | Ignores any quote characters that surround the delimiter character, and looks for the delimiter... |
| 5 | Ignores any quote characters that surround the delimiter character, and looks for the delimiter... |
ARRAYSPLIT.example:
drop program ccl_arraysplit_exam go
create program ccl_arraysplit_exam

record rec(
 1 qual[*]
   2 str = vc
)
declare num = i4 with protect
declare idx = i4 with protect  ;variable needs to be declared prior to calling arraysplit

set num = ArraySplit(rec->qual[idx].str,idx,"one;two;three;four;five;six", ';')
call echorecord(rec)
; ...

params.name: integer
params.description: Any whole number.

BLOBGET.summary: This command allows fetching long, longraw, blob, and clob data types, which exceed 32k. It returns the length of a portion of the blob that is fetched. When using the BlobGet( ) function, the WITH RDBARRAYFETCH=1 control option is added implicitly if it is not used explicitly. If sorting is performed by the query that uses the BLOBGET() function, it must be done by the RDBMS. Sorting done at the Discern Explorer level is not allowed.

params.name: Out_Buffer
params.description: A character data type variable. Generally a fixed-length character variable is used. If a VC variable is used, it must be initialized to a value with a text length greater than zero before being passed to the BlobGet function.

params.name: Offset
params.description: An integer value. Offset begins at 0 (zero).

params.name: Blob_Attribute
params.description: A long, longraw, blob, or clob data type field or value.

BLOBGET.example:
; ...
	retlen = 1
	stat = memrealloc(outbuf,1,build("C",bloblen))
	retlen = blobget(outbuf,offset,l.long_text)
	cnt = 0
	while (offset < bloblen and cnt < 100)
		cnt = cnt +1
        col 20, call print(substring(offset, 200,outbuf)), row+1
        offset = offset + 200
	endwhile
with rdbarrayfetch=1
	,maxcol=250
	,maxrec = 10

BLOBGETLEN.summary: Returns the total length of a long, longraw, blob, or clob data type. The WITH RDBARRAYFETCH = 1 control option is implicitly set if it is not used explicitly. If the query that uses the BLOBGETLEN() performs a sort, the sort must be done at the RDBMS level. Sorting done at the Discern Explorer level is not allowed.

params.name: Blob_Attribute
params.description: A long, longraw, blob, or clob data type field or value.

BLOBGETLEN.example:
select into "NL:"
	lb.long_blob_id
	,lb.long_blob
from long_blob lb
plan lb where lb.long_blob_id = $ID
detail
    outbuf = " "
    imageDataSize = blobgetlen(lb.long_blob)  ;fetch full length of blob
    stat = MEMREALLOC(outbuf,1,build("C",imageDataSize))
    fullblob = blobget(outbuf,0,lb.long_blob)
with rdbarrayfetch=1

BNOT.summary: BNOT () returns an integer expression that is the result of each bit in the base-2 number of the integer being reversed. This means that the BNOT( ) function changes all one bits to zeros, and zero bits to ones. Additionally, BNOT( ) changes the sign bit. If the value of the sign bit is zero, the integer is positive. If the sign bit value is one, the integer is negative.

params.name: Integer
params.description: Any whole number.

BOR.summary: The BOR( ) function returns an integer expression that is the result of a bit_number to bit_number or a comparison of two integers in base-2. The bit_number is the position of a bit in a field.

params.name: Integer
params.description: Any whole number.

BOX.summary: The CALL BOX command draws a box on the terminal screen for a Discern Explorer screen application program.

params.name: begin_col
params.description: The beginning column number (from 1 to 80 for 80-column mode and from 1 to 132 for 132-column mode) on the screen where the reverse-video box, scroll window, line, box, or text will be displayed.

params.name: begin_row
params.description: The beginning row number (from 1 to 24) on the screen where the box, reverse-video box, text, line, or scroll window will be displayed.

params.name: end_col
params.description: The ending column number (from 1 to 80 for 80-column mode and from 1 to 132 for 132-column mode) on the screen where the scroll window or box will be displayed.

params.name: end_row

BSHIFT.summary: Introduced in version 8.11.5 of Discern Explorer , BSHIFT() performs a bit shift operation on an integer (I4, W8) expression.

params.name: Integer
params.description: An integer (I4, W8) value.

BSHIFT.example:
call echo(bshift(32,1))   ;returns 64
  call echo(bshift(32,2))   ;returns 128
  call echo(bshift(32,-1))  ;returns 16
  call echo(bshift(32,-2))  ;returns 8

BTEST.summary: The BTEST( ) function returns an integer expression that is a one if the bit_number position of the base-2 conversion of the integer is a one. Likewise, zero is returned if the bit_number position of the base-2 conversion of the integer is a zero. The bit_number is the position of a bit in a field.

params.name: Integer
params.description: Any whole number.

params.name: Bit_position
params.description: The number of the integer position, working from right to left.

BUILD.summary: The BUILD( ) function returns an expression concatenated, with trailing blanks removed; integer and real values are treated as strings. The function acts as a concatenate function for combining character expressions with numeric expressions. Discern Explorer version 8.12.3 increases the semantic check length from 20 to 24 characters when the BUILD() function is used to pass a parameter with an F8 datatype as an argument to a subroutine call.

params.name: Expression
params.description: A value of any data type.

BUILD2.summary: The BUILD2( ) function allows you to return an expression concatenated with integer and real values treated as strings. The function acts as a concatenate function for combining character expressions with numeric expressions while maintaining leading and trailing spaces for character strings. Float values are converted to a right justified 14 character string rounded to two decimal places.

params.name: Expression
params.description: A value of any data type.

BUILD2CHK.summary: The BUILD2CHK() function allows you to return an expression concatenated with integer and reals values treated as strings. The function acts as a concatenate function for combining character expressions with numeric expressions while maintaining leading and trailing spaces for character strings. Float values are converted to a right justified 14 character string rounded to two decimal places.

params.name: expression
params.description: A value of any data type.

BUILD2CHK.example:
set text = build2chk("The number ",           99999.1, " does not exceed the max of 14 characters for an f8") go
call echo(text) go

BUILD3.summary: The BUILD3() function allows you to return a concatenated expression based on the mode, with integer and float (numeric) values converted to strings. Float values are rounded to two decimal places. Float values are displayed using up to 14 characters including the decimal point. Integer values are displayed using up to 11 characters.

params.name: expression
params.description: A value of any data type

BUILD3.table:
| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Do not remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. |
| 2 | Do not remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. |
| 3 | Remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. If a converted numeric expression exceeds 14... |
| 4 | Remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. If a converted numeric expression exceeds 14... |
BUILD3.example:
drop program ccl_test_build3 go
create program ccl_test_build3
for(mode_cnt = 1 to 4)
    call echo(BUILD3(mode_cnt, "Mode:", mode_cnt, " ", "ABC ",12.3456," ", "DEFG",789," HIJ ", 789.123, " KLM ", 123456789012345.123))
endfor
end go
ccl_test_build3 go

CALL.summary: Invokes a Discern Explorer CALL command (e.g., CALL ECHO, CALL PARSER, CALL ECHORECORD) or a user-defined SUBROUTINE without capturing a return value.

CALL ACCEPT.summary: The CALL ACCEPT command accepts input from a user in a Discern Explorer program that controls the screen display. The value accepted as a result of the CALL ACCEPT is stored in a special variable called CURACCEPT. CALL ACCEPT takes advantage of VT terminal emulation keys, such as Help, PF1, and PF2.

params.name: begin_col
params.description: The beginning column number (from 1 to 80 for an 80-column mode, and from 1 to 132 for a 132-column mode) on the screen on which the reverse-video box, scroll window, line, box, or text will be displayed.

params.name: begin_row
params.description: The beginning row number (from 1 to 24) on the screen on which the box, reverse-video box, text, line, or scroll window will be displayed.

params.name: default
params.description: The value that is displayed and entered automatically if the user presses <Return> without entering any information in the input field.

params.name: modifier
params.description: Options that enable the user to change the accepted input into another format. You must use a modifier if your picture contains anything other than 9 or N .

params.name: picture
params.description: The edit mask for one character that is accepted from the user. The following values are valid:

params.name: qualification
params.description: A condition that limits the number of records to be displayed as valid matches. Qualifications can include IF, IN, and CASE statements, and can be combined using the qualifiers AND, OR, NOT, and BETWEEN.

params.name: relational_operator
params.description: Identifies the condition in a qualification. To view valid operators, see Relational Operators.

CALL ACCEPT.table:

| --- | --- |

CALL CANCEL.summary: The CALL CANCEL command is used to stop the processing of result rows in the reportwriter clauses of a Discern Explorer Select command. Call Cancel does not immediately break out of the reportwriter clauses. Instead it attempts to perform a controlled exit out of the reportwriter clauses. When selecting from an RDBMS table and using an IF command to conditionally issue CALL CANCEL, you must use an RDBMS condition.

params.name: cancel_mode
params.description: Determines the cancel mode to be used.

CALL CANCEL.table:
| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Cancel processing of result rows. |
CALL CANCEL.example:
; ...
;;; if(pcnt = 5);this will not work call cancel requires RDBMS condition when selecting from an RDBMS table
    if(p.person_id = 5.0) ;this works because it is an RDBMS condition
        call cancel(1)
    endif
    ;call cancel will display 1 detail row for person_id 5.0
    ;the foot p.person_id and foot report will then display
    col 10 "detail"
    col +1 p.person_id
    row +1
foot p.person_id
    col 0 "foot id", col +1 p.person_id row +1
foot report
; ...

CALL DCL.summary: The CALL DCL command enables you to execute a back-end operating system command. CALL DCL spawns an operating system subprocess. The command is executed in that subprocess. Other than the status or dclstatus, no information is returned to Discern Explorer . The operating system command can direct output to a file. The DEFINE and SELECT commands, or the CCLIO function, can be used to read the file.

params.name: command
params.description: The operating system command to execute. Discern Explorer imposes a limit of 512 characters for the command including one character for the null terminator character.

params.name: length
params.description: The length of the command.

params.name: dclstatus
params.description: A variable that is set to 1 if the DCL command is successful. If the DCL command causes an error dclstatus is set to the errno status from the DCL command multiplied by 256.

CALL DCL.table:
| errno | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Operation not permitted |
| 2 | No such file or directory |
| 3 | No such process |
| 4 | Interrupted system call |
| 5 | I/O error |
| 6 | No such device or address |
| 7 | Argument list too long |
| 8 | Exec format error |
| 9 | Bad file number |
| 10 | No child processes |
| 11 | Try again |
| 12 | Out of memory |
| ... |  |
CALL DCL.example:
SET DCLCOM = "SUBMIT/KEEP/NOTIFY/QUEUE=LAB$BATCH CCLBATCH1.COM"
SET LEN = SIZE(TRIM(DCLCOM))
SET STATUS = 0
CALL DCL(DCLCOM,LEN,STATUS)

CALL ECHO.summary: The CALL ECHO command echoes an expression to the displayer, log file, or listing file. The CURECHO variable is used to compare to the echo_level. If the echo_level is less than CURECHO, the CALL ECHO command is not performed. CURECHO is reset to 0 at the start of a parent ekmodule or program. If ECHO trace is not active, CALL ECHO commands are ignored.

params.name: echo_expression
params.description: An expression to be echoed.

params.name: print_indicator
params.description: A numeric value of 0 or 1 used to determine if a new line character is printed. A value of 0 overrides the default of 1 and allows multiple CALL ECHO's to display on the same line. The print_indicator is optional.

params.name: echo_level
params.description: A numeric value. The expression is only echoed if echo_level is greater than or equal to CURECHO.

CALL ECHO.example:
SET CURECHO = 3	; change level from 0 to 3
CALL ECHO("TEST1",1,4)	; issue the call echo

The XVERTICAL option draws an extended vertical line that contains a crossbar at each end.

CALL SCROLLDOWN.summary: The CALL SCROLLDOWN command controls the way a scroll window reacts when a user presses the DOWN arrow. CALL SCROLLDOWN determines whether Discern Explorer advances to the next line in the scroll box or moves the top line of the scroll window out of the box and moves the next available line not in the scroll window to the bottom of the box.

params.name: current_row
params.description: The row that is selected as a result of the user pressing the DOWN arrow.

params.name: Expression
params.description: An expression is the highest-level metasymbol among constants, field names, variables, and so on. The following expressions are valid:

params.name: previous_row
params.description: The last row that was selected before the user pressed the DOWN arrow.

CALL SCROLLDOWN.example:
IF (CNT < MAXCNT)
SET CNT = CNT + 1
	IF (AROW = NUMSROW)
	CALL SCROLLDOWN(NUMSROW,NUMSROW,BUFFER[CNT])	;scroll bottom of window
	ELSE
	SET AROW = AROW + 1
CALL SCROLLDOWN(AROW-1,AROW,BUFFER[CNT])	;scroll above bottom
ENDIF
ENDIF

CALL SCROLLINIT.summary: The CALL SCROLLINIT command tells Discern Explorer that a scroll window is used in the display. To change between multiple scroll windows, issue a CALL SCROLLINIT command to establish the current scroll window followed by CALL SCROLLTEXT to display text to the current scroll window. Use the CALL BOX command to display a box around the scroll window.

CALL SCROLLTEXT.summary: The CALL SCROLLTEXT command displays information on a row in a scroll window in normal video mode. For screen displays, normal mode is bold letters (intense) displayed in the default font and pitch for your terminal. The most common use of this command is to refresh a scroll window with new information once the PF1 or NEXT SCREEN key is pressed.
CALL SCROLLTEXT.example:
; ...

SET CNT = CNT + 1
CALL SCROLLTEXT(AROW,BUFFER[CNT])
SET AROW = AROW + 1

ENDWHILE

SET AROW = 1

SET CNT = CNT - NUMSROW + 1

ENDIF

CALL SCROLLUP.summary: The CALL SCROLLUP command controls the way a scroll window reacts when a user presses the UP arrow. This command determines whether Discern Explorer backs up to the previous line in the scroll box, or moves the bottom line of the scroll window out of the box and moves the next available line not in the scroll window to the top of the box.
CALL SCROLLUP.example:
IF (CNT > 1)
SET CNT = CNT - 1
IF (AROW = 1)
CALL SCROLLUP(AROW,AROW,BUFFER[CNT]) ;scroll top of window
ELSE
SET AROW = AROW - 1
CALL SCROLLUP(AROW+1,AROW,BUFFER[CNT]) ;scroll below top of window
ENDIF
ENDIF

CASE.summary: The CASE command compares a CASE expression to the OF expressions and performs actions when a match is found. At least one case_item is required. If multiple OF expressions are true.     ELSE: SET label = "Unknown"

CCLIO.summary: CCLIO( ) provides access to streaming input and output (IO) functions.
CCLIO.table:
| Function Name | Description | Input/Output/Notes: Depending on the Function_Name That is Specified, the CCLIO() Function Uses... | Return: The CCLIO() Function Returns Different Values Depending on the Function_Name That is Used. |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| "CLOSE" | Close the file and commit its contents to disk. | Input(record_name->file_desc) | 0: close error 1: close success |
| "EOF" | Return end of file. | Input(record_name->file_desc) | 0: not end of file 1: end of file reached |
| "ERROR" | Return error messages. | Input(record_name->file_desc) | 0: error 1: success |
| "FLUSH" | Commits file contents to disk. | Input(record_name->file_desc) | 0: flush error 1: flush success |
| "GETS" | Read from file using a record operation. | Input(record_name->file_desc, record_name->file_buf) | 0: gets error 1: gets success |
| "OPEN" | Open the file and set the open mode. | The record_name->file_buf field is used to specify the open mode. | 0: open error 1: open success |
| "PUTS" | Write to file use a record operation | Input(record_name->file_desc, record_name->file_buf) | 0: puts error 1: puts success |
| "READ" | Read entire file | Input(record_name->file_desc) Output( record_name->file_buf) | Number of bytes read |
| "SEEK" | Find a location in the file | Input(record_name->file_desc, record_name->file_offset, record_name->file_dir) Note: if... | 0: seek error 1: seek success |
| "SHOW" | Shows list of all open file descriptors | Input(record_name->file_desc) | 0: show error 1: show success |
| "TELL" | Return current position for open file | Input(record_name->file_desc) | Current position for open file |
| "WRITE" | Write entire file | Input(record_name->file_desc, record_name->file_buf) | Number of bytes written |
CCLIO.example:
; ...
   SET FREC->FILE_NAME = "CCL_TEST.DAT"
   SET FREC->FILE_BUF = "r" /* file_buf values are case sensitive so lowercase r is used */
   SET STAT = CCLIO("OPEN",FREC)
    ;Allocate buffer for desired read size
   SET FREC->FILE_BUF = NOTRIM(FILLSTRING(132," "))
   IF (FREC->FILE_DESC != 0)
       SET STAT = 1
       WHILE (STAT > 0)
	;read the file one record at a time
          SET STAT = CCLIO("GETS",FREC)
          IF (STAT > 0)
              SET POS = FINDSTRING(CHAR(0),FREC->FILE_BUF)
              SET POS = EVALUATE(POS,0,SIZE(FREC->FILE_BUF),POS)
              CALL ECHO(SUBSTRING(1,POS,FREC->FILE_BUF))
          ENDIF
; ...

CCLREGEXP.summary: CCLREGEXP( ) provides regular expression pattern matching. Discern Explorer versions 8.13.0 and 9.01.0 introduced LIKE, FIND, and COUNT modes. Discern Explorer versions 8.17.4 and 9.05.4 resolve memory issue for FIND|COUNT mode when total size of search and pattern strings exceed 1000 characters. CCLREGEXP( ) uses the Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX) metacharacter set for regular expression pattern matching.
CCLREGEXP.example:
; ...
set offset = 1
while(offset != 0 )
    set offset = cclregexp("FIND",recreg)
    if(offset != 0)
        call echo(concat("Occurrence "
                            , trim(cnvtstring(recreg->occ))
                            , " of '"
                            , recreg->pat
                            , "' was found at offset "
                            , trim(cnvtstring(offset))
                            , "."))
        set recreg->occ +=1
    endif
; ...

CLASSREF.summary: The CLASSREF() function has multiple modes, and is used to create a reference to a class instance or save the address to a class instance used to reference a class instance in the future. The function returns 0 for an error, 1 for success. The CLASSREF function was introduced in Discern Explorer version 8.11.3. Discern Explorer versions 8.13.2 and 9.01.2 introduce the ability to pass a class instance by reference.

params.description: The address for a reference from a class instance.

params.name: classins_addr_to
params.description: The address for a reference to a class instance.

params.name: classins_from
params.description: The name of the class instance creating a reference for.

params.name: classins_ref_to
params.description: The name of the reference that refers to a class instance.

CLASSREF.table:
| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | set classins_ref_to = classins_from |
| 2 | set classins_addr_to = classins_from |
| 3 | set classins_ref_to = classins_addr_from |
| 4 | clear classins_ref_to |
| 5 | set classins_addr_to = curinstance (used in the class definition to get the current instance... |
CLASSREF.example:
; ...
  declare gcnt = i4
  declare i_genarray[2] = i4
  set stat = classref(i_genarray[1],m1::i_rush,2)        ;save generic instance ref in array for class instance
  set stat = classref(i_genarray[2],m1::i_cheaptrick,2)  ;save generic instance ref in array for class instance
  for (gcnt=1 to size(i_genarray,5))
       if (i_genarray[gcnt] and classref(m1::i_gen,i_genarray[gcnt],3) != 0) ;set generic instance ref to class instance ref
           call echo(build(">>>generic array classref=",gcnt))
           call m1::i_gen.show(2)
       endif
  endfor
  if (classref(m1::i_gen,m1::i_rush) != 0)  ;set generic instance ref to class instance
      call echo(build(">>>generic var classref"))
      call m1::i_gen.show(2)
  endif
; ...

or

DCL.summary: The CALL DCL command enables you to execute a back-end operating system command. CALL DCL spawns an operating system subprocess. The command is executed in that subprocess. Other than the status or dclstatus, no information is returned to Discern Explorer . The operating system command can direct output to a file. The DEFINE and SELECT commands, or the CCLIO function, can be used to read the file.

params.description: The operating system command to execute. Discern Explorer imposes a limit of 512 characters for the command including one character for the null terminator character.

params.name: length
params.description: The length of the command.

params.name: dclstatus
params.description: A variable that is set to 1 if the DCL command is successful. If the DCL command causes an error dclstatus is set to the errno status from the DCL command multiplied by 256.

| --- | --- |
| 1 | Operation not permitted |
| 2 | No such file or directory |
| 3 | No such process |
| 4 | Interrupted system call |
| 5 | I/O error |
| 6 | No such device or address |
| 7 | Argument list too long |
| 8 | Exec format error |
| 9 | Bad file number |
| 10 | No child processes |
| 11 | Try again |
| 12 | Out of memory |
| ... |  |
DCL.example:
SET DCLCOM = "SUBMIT/KEEP/NOTIFY/QUEUE=LAB$BATCH CCLBATCH1.COM"
SET LEN = SIZE(TRIM(DCLCOM))
SET STATUS = 0
CALL DCL(DCLCOM,LEN,STATUS)

DECODE( ) can be used to determine which side of the ORJOIN a row in the result set is from or if the row in the result set contains values from the DONTCARE or OUTERJOIN tables. DECODE( ) returns the first result following a table_name.column_name value that is not a placeholder in the result set.

The file name must be enclosed in quotes and follow the operating system's file-naming conventions.

DELETE.summary: The DELETE command deletes existing rows in a table. Only authorized Oracle personnel should use the DELETE command on Oracle production tables. The FROM clause is required when using the DELETE command. You must also use the WHERE clause to qualify which records should be deleted. To delete all records, use the wild card option as part of your qualification or add seq = 1.

params.name: delete_option

DENSE_RANK.summary: The DENSE_RANK( ) function returns a ranking number for each value in a group of rows. DENSE_RANK( ) can be used in the select list as an OLAP expression using the OVER( ) clause if using Discern Explorer version 8.8.0 or higher and Oracle 10g or higher. DENSE_RANK( ) requires an ORDER BY in the OVER( ) clause. Rows with the same value are given the same rank. The next rank is the next sequential value.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest level metasymbol among constants, column names, variables, and so on.

params.name: exp_name
params.description: The name to use as the column heading and select expression of the value returned by the DENSE_RANK() function.

DENSE_RANK.example:
SELECT
	E.PERSON_ID
	, E.REG_DT_TM
	, E.ENCNTR_ID
	, P_RANK = RANK() OVER( ORDER BY E.PERSON_ID )
	, P_DENSE_RANK = DENSE_RANK() OVER( ORDER BY E.PERSON_ID )
	, E_ENCNTR_TYPE_CLASS_DISP = UAR_GET_CODE_DISPLAY(E.ENCNTR_TYPE_CLASS_CD)

FROM
	ENCOUNTER   E

WHERE E.REG_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTLOOKBEHIND("2,W") AND CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE,CURTIME3)
; ...

DETAIL.summary: The DETAIL clause lets Discern Explorer work with report items at their lowest level, which may be one column for a row, or one column from an array of columns for a row. The DETAIL clause enables Discern Explorer to work through the data one row at a time. The syntax of the DETAIL clause is shown below: Keep these points in mind when using the DETAIL clause: The DETAIL clause is optional.

DM14.summary: 14-byte used for timestamp with time zone (Usage: T)

DONTCARE.summary: This topic discusses the Discern Explorer DONTCARE Control Option. Only use the Discern Explorer DONTCARE Control Option when reading Non-RDBMS tables. If working with all RDBMS tables, use the OUTERJOIN() function or a LEFT JOIN in the From clause of the SELECT command. See JOIN Options for more information on available join options. The Discern Explorer DONTCARE joins are useful only when you have joins between three or more tables.

JOIN D2
JOIN PN	WHERE M.PERSON_ID = PN.PERSON_ID

ECHO.summary: The CALL ECHO command echoes an expression to the displayer, log file, or listing file. The CURECHO variable is used to compare to the echo_level. If the echo_level is less than CURECHO, the CALL ECHO command is not performed. CURECHO is reset to 0 at the start of a parent ekmodule or program. If ECHO trace is not active, CALL ECHO commands are ignored.

params.name: echo_expression
params.description: An expression to be echoed.

params.name: print_indicator
params.description: A numeric value of 0 or 1 used to determine if a new line character is printed. A value of 0 overrides the default of 1 and allows multiple CALL ECHO's to display on the same line. The print_indicator is optional.

params.name: echo_level
params.description: A numeric value. The expression is only echoed if echo_level is greater than or equal to CURECHO.

ECHO.example:
SET CURECHO = 3	; change level from 0 to 3
CALL ECHO("TEST1",1,4)	; issue the call echo
CALL ECHO("TEST1",1,2)	; ignore the call echo
CALL ECHO("TEST")
CALL ECHO("PROC SELECT")
CALL ECHO(BUILD("NUM_QUAL",CURQUAL) )

ECHORECORD.summary: The CALL ECHORECORD command echos the contents of a record structure to the displayer, the default log, listing file, to a user-defined filename. Before Discern Explorer versions 8.14.1 and 9.02.1, CALL ECHORECORD accepted a record structure name and echoed the entire contents of the record structure.

params.name: Record_name
params.description: Name of the record structure.

params.name: Record_member

params.name: Output_name

| 1 | Append new information to the existing output_name file |

CALL ECHORECORD(ORDERS_REC)

END
GO

Before Discern Explorer versions 8.14.1 and 9.02.1, CALL ECHORECORD accepted a record structure name and echoed the entire contents of the record structure.

params.name: record_member

ERROR.summary: The ERROR( ) function returns the error code from the error that is on top of the Error stack. It returns 0 if the Error stack does not contain any errors. Discern Explorer maintains an Error stack for each program execution. The error stack contains up to five errors. If more than five errors occur, the error stack contains the first four errors and the last error that occurred in the program.

params.name: errmsg
params.description: A C132, or VC data type variable or record item. The text of the error message is assigned to errmsg .

params.name: flag
params.description: A constant or variable that determines whether the Error stack is reset. The following values are valid:

| Value | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Do not reset the stack. |
| 1 | Reset the stack. |
ERROR.example:
DECLARE ERRMSG = C132
DECLARE ERRCODE = I4 WITH NOCONSTANT(1)
WHILE (ERRCODE != 0)
     SET ERRCODE = ERROR(ERRMSG,0) ;don't reset error stack
     CALL ECHO(BUILD("Error number:",ERRCODE))
     CALL ECHO(ERRMSG)
ENDWHILE

EVALUATE.summary: The EVALUATE( ) function allows you to return an expression based on a condition. Similar functionality is used with the CASE or IF commands.

params.name: case_expr
params.description: An expression that is being compared to the case_value.

params.name: case_value
params.description: A value that is compared to the case_expr. If the condition is true, the return_value is returned.

params.name: return_value
params.description: The value that is returned if the case_expr is equal to the case_value. The final return_value is used as a default if none of the conditions are true.

EVALUATE2.summary: The EVALUATE2 () function returns the result of an IF() statement as a function call. Similar to the EVALUATE() function, the EVALUATE2() function is more powerful in that it allows relational operators to be used in the IF() clause.

params.name: if_clause
params.description: A valid IF() clause.

EVALUATE2.example:
; ...
, P_POSITION_DISP = UAR_GET_CODE_DISPLAY(P.POSITION_CD)
, P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED
, POSITION_TYPE = EVALUATE2(
IF(P.POSITION_CD = RN_VAR
OR P.POSITION_CD = LPN_VAR) "NURSE"
ELSEIF(P.POSITION_CD = RES_VAR
OR P.POSITION_CD = PATH_VAR) "DOC  "
ENDIF)
FROM PRSNL P
WHERE P.POSITION_CD IN (LPN_VAR, RN_VAR, RES_VAR, PATH_VAR)
WITH NOCOUNTER, SEPARATOR=" ", FORMAT

EXPAND.summary: The EXPAND( ) function creates a qualification in the query that is passed to the Relational Database Management System (RDBMS). It is generally used to compare the values from a Level 1 record structure list item to a field on an RDBMS table. A 1 is returned if at least one item in the Record Member Item list is equal to the search expression. By default, an IN clause is created in the query that is passed to the RDBMS.

params.description: An integer data type variable. When Expand() is used in a SELECT command, the index_variable must be declared before the Select.

params.description: The position of the record structure list that contains the first value to be used in the qualification.

params.name: index_end
params.description: The position of the record structure list that contains the last value to be used in the qualification.

For example, to create a line that is 60 characters long, instead of typing the underscore character (_) 60 times, you can use the FILLSTRING( ) function as shown in the below example. You then can call the expression any number of times in your query.

params.name: literal_char
params.description: A one-character literal. Quotation marks are required.

params.description: The file name to be searched for. By default, Discern Explorer looks for the file in CCLUSERDIR, unless a path for the file location is included in the file_name .

| 1 | Find file using exact match of file name on Unix domains else uppercase file on AXP domains. |

The start_pos can be used to perform a search for the next occurrence of the search text. The FINDSTRING( ) function is case-sensitive, therefore only like characters are found. When no matches are found, a zero is returned.

params.name: search_expression
params.description: The text expression to be searched for.

params.name: source_expression
params.description: The source text in which the search expression should be located.

params.name: start_pos

params.description: An expression that is a real number.

FOOT PAGE.summary: The FOOT PAGE clause enables you to print a page footer and perform report items at the end of each page. The report items in the FOOT PAGE clause are executed when the maximum number of rows (MAXROW) has been printed or a BREAK command is encountered. The syntax of the FOOT PAGE clause is shown below:
FOOT PAGE.example:
FOOT PAGE
	ROW 57
	COL 0 LINE_S
	ROW 58
	COL 0 "This report created by the Discern Explorer Program:"
        COL +1 CURPROG
	ROW 59
	COL 0 LINE_S

FOOT REPORT.summary: The FOOT REPORT clause is used to perform report items at the end of a report, like printing a summary page. Keep these points in mind when using the FOOT REPORT clause: The FOOT REPORT clause is optional; If a FOOT REPORT clause is used a HEAD REPORT clause must also be used; A SELECT command can include only one FOOT REPORT clause; A FOOT REPORT clause must include at least one report item.
FOOT REPORT.example:
FOOT REPORT
	ROW +5
	CALL CENTER("*** Grand Totals For Report ***",0,120)
	ROW +1
	COL 62 "Total number of days: "
	COL 95 SUM(LOS)
	ROW +1
	COL 62 "Total number of patients: "
	COL 95 COUNT(NAME)
	ROW +1
	COL 62 "Total Patients with LOS > 5: "
	COL 95 COUNT(NAME WHERE LOS >5)
; ...

FOR.summary: The FOR command is used to process a block of Discern Explorer commands multiple times. The FOR command sets the variable equal to the value of integer1, executes the for_items, then increments the variable by the increment value if the BY increment is used. If the BY increment is not used, the variable is incremented by one. After the increment is performed, the FOR command checks to see if the variable is greater than the value of integer2.

params.name: for_item
params.description: A command or instruction performed by a FOR statement. Valid FOR items are commands and report items. A command is a Discern Explorer instruction that can be executed by itself (for example, BROWSE, CREATE TABLE, DROP PROGRAM, and SELECT) or...

params.description: A whole number that is the beginning value to be assigned to the variable by the FOR loop.

params.name: integer2
params.description: A whole number that is the ending value to be assigned to the variable by the FOR loop.

params.name: increment
params.description: A whole number that is used to increment the variable in the FOR loop.

params.name: variable
params.description: A variable name. If the variable name does not already exist, it is created by default.

    CALL ECHO(rec->list[idx].name)
ENDFOR

FORMAT.summary: FORMAT( ) transforms an expression into a string using a user-specified format. The format is made up of three elements; the display_template, display_qualifier, and display_format, enclosed in quotations marks. The elements are separated by a semicolon (;). At least one of the elements is required. If the display_template is not used, a leading semicolon must be used as a placeholder.

params.name: expression
params.description: The item to format.

MIN.syntax:
MIN(expression [WHERE qualification]) ["template;display_qualifier;display_format"]
exp_name = MIN([param{,param}]) [KEEP(DENSE_RANK FIRST|LAST ORDER BY expression[DESC])]
  OVER (
  [PARTITION BY expression{,expression}]
  [ORDER BY expression[DESC],{expression[DESC]}]
  [RANGE|ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED|int PRECEDING  |  UNBOUNDED|int FOLLOWING  |  CURRENT ROW
          AND BETWEEN UNBOUNDED|int PRECEDING  |  UNBOUNDED|int FOLLOWING  |  CURRENT ROW ]
      )
MIN.summary: The MIN ( ) function displays the smallest value of an expression across a specified break. MIN( ) can be used in the FOOT REPORT or FOOT group_expression sections of a Discern Explorer Select command to calculate the minimum of a numeric (float, integer, or datetime) expression.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest level metasymbol among constants, column names, variables, and so on.

params.name: exp_name
params.description: The name to use as the column heading and select expression of the value returned by the MIN() function.

params.name: int
params.description: An integer value.

MIN.example:
; ...
	ROW +1
FOOT C.ENCNTR_ID
	COL 10 "Min Temp:"
	COL +1 MIN(TEMP_REAL) "###.##"
	ROW +1
WITH NOCOUNTER, SEPARATOR=" ", FORMAT

MINUTE.summary: The MINUTE( ) function allows you to return the minute component of time, which is in (HHMM) format or a rdb_dt_tm column. A real number from 0 to 60.00 is returned.

params.name: time
params.description: An expression that typically is in the format HHMM.

params.name: rdb_dt_tm
params.description: A column that stores the date and time.

MINUTE.example:
drop program hhtest go
create program hhtest
select
ACTIVE_STATUS_DT_TM ";;q",
	minute = minute(P.ACTIVE_STATUS_DT_TM)
from person p
with maxrec = 100
end
go

MINVAL.summary: The MINVAL() function allows you to return the smallest expression from the list of expressions.

params.name: numeric_expr
params.description: An expression that is an integer or a real number.

MINVAL.example:
drop program hhtest go
create program hhtest
set first = 71
set second = 20
set third = 51
set fourth = 40
set fifth = 37
select
	result = minval(first,second,third,fourth,fifth)
from dummyt
end
go

MOD.summary: Returns an integer that is the remainder of the first integer divided by the second integer (mod_value).

params.name: integer
params.description: Any whole number or an expression that is an integer.

params.name: mod_value
params.description: An integer or variable divided into an integer expression to produce a whole number remainder.

MOD.example:
; ...
col 5 "RESULT:" COL 25 "RESULT CODE:"
ROW + 1
 rec_code = mod(RESULT,value)
 col 5 result col 25 rec_code
 row + 1
with maxrec = 50
end
go

MODCHECK.summary: The MODCHECK() function allows you to return the result of a checksum on the integer expression in expression. Valid values for integer are 10 (for checksum10) and 43 (for checksum43). Oracle uses this function primarily in bar-coding programs.

params.name: integer
params.description: Any whole number.

MODIFY.summary: MODIFY( ) returns 1 if the modify option is on, and returns 0 if the modify option is off.

params.name: modify_option
params.description: An option that can be set using the SET MODIFY command.

MODIFY.example:
call echo(modify("SPOOLFILE")) GO
SET MODIFY SPOOLFILE GO
call echo(modify("SPOOLFILE")) GO

MONTH.summary: The MONTH() function allows you to return the integer month of a Julian date or an rdb_date_time column. An integer from 1 to 12 is returned.

params.name: julian_date
params.description: An expression that is an Internal System Date.

params.name: rdb_date_time
params.description: A column that stores a datetime or function that returns a datetime.

MONTH.example:
select
	date = P.ACTIVE_STATUS_DT_TM,
	active_month = month(P.ACTIVE_STATUS_DT_TM),
	cur_month = month(curdate),
	fun_month = month(cnvtdatetime(curdate,curtime3)),
	aug_month = month(cnvtdate(08152023))
from
	person p
with maxrec = 10

MOVEREC.summary: The MOVEREC ( ) function performs the following A record structure is defined with the RECORD command. The names of the items in the record structures can be different but the layout and data types of the items must be the same.

params.name: record_name
params.description: The name of a record structure that previously was defined using the record command or the name of the record that Discern Explorer generates a definition in the Discern Explorer Data Dictionary.

params.name: record_segment
params.description: A record structure item that was defined with a dimension in the Record command. In the Record command, an item at any level that is given a name followed by square brackets, enclosing an asterisk or integer but not assigned a data type is a record...

params.name: table_name
params.description: The name of the table from the Discern Explorer Data Dictionary or an alias defined in the From clause for a table.

MOVERECLIST.syntax: MOVERECLIST(from_record_list, to_record_list, from_list_index, to_list_index, num_occurs, insert_mode)
MOVERECLIST.summary: The MOVERECLIST() function allows you to move values from one or more positions in one record structure list, into a list in another record structure or into a different list in the same record structure. Do not use MOVERECLIST() to move values from one position in a list to another position in the same list in the same record structure. Doing so results in loss of data or other unexpected results.

params.name: from_record_list
params.description: A record structure list that contains the values to be moved. In the Record command, an item at any level that is given a name, followed by square brackets enclosing an asterisk (*) or an integer but not assigned a data type is a record list.

params.name: to_record_list
params.description: A record structure list, with a definition that matches the from_record_list.

params.name: from_list_index
params.description: An integer value representing the position of the from_record_list that contains the values to be moved.

params.name: to_list_index
params.description: An integer value representing the position of the to_record_list to which the values are moved. If False is used for the insert_mode, the values are moved to the position of the to_record_list specified by the to_list_index.

params.name: num_occurs
params.description: The number of positions to move from the from_record_list to the to_record_list.

params.name: insert_mode
params.description: True (1): Insert the values from the from_record_list into the to_record_list. When using true, the size of the to_record_list is increased by the num_occurs value and the from_record_list values are inserted after the to_list_index position.

MOVESTRING.summary: The MOVESTRING () function copies a character expression into another character expression and returns the number of characters that were copied. The first string expression, starting at the position indicated by source_start, is moved to the second string expression, starting at the position indicated by target_start. The number of characters moved is specified by length.

params.name: source_start
params.description: An integer that defines the beginning position in the source_text.

params.name: target_start
params.description: An integer that defines the beginning position in the target_text.

params.name: length
params.description: An integer that defines the number of characters to copy.

MPAGES_EVENT.summary: The MPAGES_EVENT routine allows you to evoke special conversation events from in a web page.

params.name: eventname
params.description: A textual string representing the name of the conversation event that is to be triggered. The following options are valid:

MPAGES_EVENT.table:
| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| ALLERGY | This element specifies that the Allergy conversation is opened. |
| POWERFORM | This element specifies that the PowerForm PowerForm conversation is opened. |
| POWERNOTE | This element specifies that the PowerNote conversation is opened. |
| ORDERS | This element specifies that the Modal Order Entry Window is opened. |
| CLINICALNOTE | This element specifies that the Clinical Note conversation is opened. |

MPAGES_SVC_EVENT.summary: MPAGES_SVC_EVENT is a routine used to launch into the Discern MPages web service. For this routine to work, the following META tag must be included in the HEAD of the html file: <META content='MPAGES_SVC_EVENT' name='discern'>

params.name: uri
params.description: An address specifying the report to be executed.

params.name: params
params.description: The parameters for the report.

NEGATE.summary: Performs a Boolean negation on a Boolean.

params.name: boolean_expression
params.description: A Boolean expression

NOCONSTANT.summary: Initializes a mutable declared variable with the specified starting value.

NOPATSTRING.summary: NOPATSTRING () skips pattern-matching in the expression.

params.name: expression
params.description: A character data type value.

NOPATSTRING.example:
SELECT INTO "NL:"
	C.RESULT_VAL
FROM
	CLINICAL_EVENT   C
WHERE C.RESULT_VAL = NOPATSTRING("DQB1*0201")

NORDBBIND.summary: Beginning with Discern Explorer version 8.10.2, NORRDBBIND() is ignored. Before Discern Explorer version 8.10.2, NORDBBIND( ) was used to override the default behavior of bind parameters in the queries sent to the RDBMS based on the following rules: If optimizer mode is RBO, NORDBBIND() is ignored and bind variables are used in the query that is sent to the RDBMS; If optimizer mode is CBO and any non-RDBMS tables are used in the query...

params.name: expr
params.description: A value of any data type.

NORDBBIND.example:
select p.person_id
	,p.updt_dt_tm
from person p
where p.person_id = NORDBBIND(id_var)
with format, separator = " "

NOTRIM.summary: This function prevents trimming trailing spaces from a string that is assigned to a variable character data type variable or record structure item.
NOTRIM.example:
DROP PROGRAM NO_TRIM_EX GO
CREATE PROGRAM NO_TRIM_EX
RECORD REC(1 FLD1 = VC)		;auto trim trailing spaces by default
SET REC->FLD1="ABC   "
CALL ECHO(BUILD('SIZE OF REC->FLD1=',SIZE(REC->FLD1)))	;size of rec->fld1=3
SET REC->FLD1=TRIM("ABC   ")
CALL ECHO(BUILD('SIZE OF REC->FLD1=',SIZE(REC->FLD1))) 	;size of rec->fld1=3
SET REC->FLD1=NOTRIM("ABC   ")
CALL ECHO(BUILD('SIZE OF REC->FLD1=',SIZE(REC->FLD1))) 	;size of rec->fld1=6

declare vc_var = vc with protect
set vc_var = "abc  "
; ...

NTILE.summary: The NTILE( ) function divides the qualifying rows into the number of groups represented by int and assigns a number from 1 to int to each group. If 25 rows are in the partition, NTILE(4) returns four groups numbered 1 through 4. Three groups would contain six rows, and one group would contain seven rows.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest level metasymbol among constants, column names, variables, and so on.

params.name: exp_name
params.description: The name to use as the column heading and Select expression of the value returned by the NTILE( ) function.

params.name: int
params.description: An integer value.

NTILE.example:
SELECT
	P.PERSON_ID
	, NAME = SUBSTRING(1,30,P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED)
	, O.ORDER_ID
	, O.ORIG_ORDER_DT_TM "@SHORTDATETIME"
	, NTILE_4 = NTILE(4) OVER(PARTITION BY P.PERSON_ID ORDER BY O.ORIG_ORDER_DT_TM DESC)
	, NTILE_10 = NTILE(10) OVER(PARTITION BY P.PERSON_ID ORDER BY O.ORIG_ORDER_DT_TM DESC)
	, CAT_DISP = UAR_GET_CODE_DISPLAY(O.CATALOG_CD)
FROM
	PERSON   P
	, ORDERS   O
PLAN O WHERE O.ORIG_ORDER_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTLOOKBEHIND("2,W") AND  CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE ,CURTIME3)
; ...

NULL.summary: NULL () is only valid in a Report Writer clause of a SELECT that is using an ORJOIN, or the OUTERJOIN or DONTCARE control options. It returns 0 if the field contains a valid value, 1 if the field is NULL or undefined. The DECODE() function is preferred, and it should be used instead of NULL().

params.name: Field_name
params.description: A field from a table used in the ORJOIN, OUTERJOIN, or DONTCARE control options.

NULL.example:
; ...
	COL 0 P.PERSON_ID
	COL +1 E.ENCNTR_ID
	ISNULL = NULL(E.ENCNTR_ID)
	COL +1 ISNULL
	ROW +1
WITH OUTERJOIN = D

NULLCHECK.summary: The NULLCHECK () function returns the expression if nullind equals zero, otherwise it returns the default value.

params.name: expression
params.description: A value of any data type.

params.name: default
params.description: A value of any data type, but it must be consistent with the expression used.

params.name: nullind
params.description: A condition that is set to 1 if the expression is null or zero if the expression is not null.

NULLFMT.summary: The NULLFMT() function allows you to return the value from an RDBMS table.field attribute as a character value or return a character string that indicates the attribute is NULL. The display width is the larger of the formatted attribute or the null_expression. The NULLFMT() function is introduced in Discern Explorer versions 8.15.0 and 9.03.0.

params.name: attribute
params.description: An RDBMS table.field .

params.name: null_expression
params.description: A character value to return if the attribute is NULL. If the null_expression is not specified, <null> is returned.

NULLFMT.table:
| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Do not remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. |
| 2 | Do not remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. |
| 3 | Remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. If a converted numeric expression exceeds 14... |
| 4 | Remove leading spaces from numeric expressions. If a converted numeric expression exceeds 14... |
NULLFMT.example:
; ...
select into $outdev
    c.*
    ,i4_null = nullfmt(c.i4_fld)
    ,i4_null_e = nullfmt(c.i4_fld,"null_i4")
    ,i4_null_1 = nullfmt(c.i4_fld,"null_i4_1",1)
    ,i4_null_2 = nullfmt(c.i4_fld,"null_i4_2",2)
    ,i4_null_3 = nullfmt(c.i4_fld,"null_i4_3",3)
    ,i4_null_4 = nullfmt(c.i4_fld,"null_i4_4",4)

    ,f8_null = nullfmt(c.f8_fld)
    ,f8_null_e = nullfmt(c.f8_fld,"null_f8")
    ,f8_null_1 = nullfmt(c.f8_fld,"null_f8_1",1)
; ...

NULLIND.summary: The NULLIND() function checks a table column to determine a NULL value. It returns zero ( 0 ) if the value is not NULL, 1 if the value is NULL. The NULLIND() function should be used in the selection list. NULLIND() can be used in a Report Writer section, but for better performance it should be used in the Selection list.

params.name: alias
params.description: The alias assigned to a table in the From clause.

params.name: column_name
params.description: The name of a column (field) from a table.

NULLIND.example:
SELECT
     DISCHARGE_STAT = NULLIND(E.DISCH_DT_TM)
FROM ENCOUNTER E
WHERE E.REG_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTLOOKBEHIND("1,W") AND CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE,CURTIME3)
WITH NOCOUNTER

NULLTERM.summary: Null terminates a character expression. Any trailing spaces at the end of the character expression is trimmed. A binary zero is added to the end of the character string.

params.name: expression
params.description: A character value.

params.name: option
params.description: 1: Include the null terminator character (binary zero) in the length of the string.

NULLTERM.example:
DECLARE NT_NAME = VC
SET NT_NAME = NULLTERM(P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED,1)

DECLARE MEANING_VAR = C12
SET MEANING_VAR = "COMBINED"
DECLARE COMBINED_VAR = F8
SET COMBINED_VAR = UAR_GET_CODE_BY("MEANING",48,NULLTERM(MEANING_VAR))

NULLVAL.summary: NULLVAL () checks the value of expression 1. If the value is not a null value, expression 1 is returned; otherwise, expression 2 is returned.

params.name: expr1
params.description: A column from an Relational Database Management System (RDBMS) table of any data type.

params.name: expr2
params.description: A value of any data type. Expr2 should match the data type of expr1.

OPERATOR.syntax:
OPERATOR( expr, operator  {,expr } )

NOTOPERATOR( expr, operator  {,expr } )
OPERATOR.summary: The OPERATOR( ) function allows you to construct a dynamic relational clause.

params.name: expr
params.description: An expression.

params.name: operator
params.description: A relational operator.

params.name: notoperator
params.description: Negates the operator; for example, OPERATOR(expression1, != ,expression2) and NOTOPERATOR(expression1, = ,expression2) are equivalent.

OPERATOR.example:
; ...
        plan d where initarray(dseq,d.seq)
        join e where e.active_flag = "A"
        and operator(e.module_name,"LIKE",notrim(patstring(rec->qual[dseq].name,1)))
    end go

ORDERDIR.summary: ORDERDIR is used in the ORDER clause to allow dynamically flexing the direction of the sort. It was introduced in Discern Explorer version 8.7.1.

params.name: expression
params.description: A field or expression from the select list.

ORDERDIR.table:
| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Sort in ascending order |
| 1 | Sort in descending order |
ORDERDIR.example:
; ...
WHERE P.UPDT_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTLOOKBEHIND("1,D") AND CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE, CURTIME3)
    AND P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED > ","
ORDER ORDERDIR(P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED,A_D_VAR)
WITH MAXREC = 1000, NOCOUNTER, SEPARATOR=" ", FORMAT,TIME = 30

END
GO

OUTDEV.summary: Standard output device parameter ($OUTDEV) passed into CCL reports and Discern Explorer scripts.

OUTERJOIN.summary: The OUTERJOIN function allows qualifying rows on a joined table to be optional. By default, selecting fields from more than one table requires qualifying rows to exist on all tables. For example, selecting from the PERSON and ENCOUNTER tables, where the Person_ID fields are equal, requires the same Person_ID to exist on both tables.
OUTERJOIN.example:
SELECT 	P.PERSON_ID,
       	P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED,
       	C.CLINICAL_EVENT_ID,
       	C_EVENT_DISP = UAR_GET_CODE_DISPLAY(C.EVENT_CD)
FROM 	PERSON P, CLINICAL_EVENT C
WHERE 	P.UPDT_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE-7,0) AND CNVTDATETIME(SYSDATE) AND
        C.PERSON_ID = OUTERJOIN(P.PERSON_ID)

SELECT 	P.PERSON_ID,
       	P.NAME_FULL_FORMATTED,
       	C.CLINICAL_EVENT_ID,
       	C_EVENT_DISP = UAR_GET_CODE_DISPLAY(C.EVENT_CD)
; ...

PARAMETER.summary: The PARAMETER( ) function fetches the value of a parameter that is passed to a program using the Execute command. When assigning the output of the Parameter( ) function to a character data type variable, the variable must be predeclared as a VC. Assign numeric data type parameters to a variable with the same numeric data type.

params.name: Parameter number
params.description: Parameters are numbered sequentially from left to right with 1 representing the first parameter. The parameter number indicates the parameter to fetch. PARAMETER2() can be used to return the parameter number using the parameter name.

params.name: List number
params.description: Use zero (0) if the parameter is not a list. If the parameter is a list, the list number indicates which list item to fetch. List items are numbered sequentially from left to right with 1 representing the first item in the list.

PARAMETER.example:
DROP PROGRAM ccl_parameter_exam GO
CREATE PROGRAM ccl_parameter_exam
DECLARE parameter_value1 = VC
DECLARE parameter_value2_1 = VC
DECLARE parameter_value2_2 = VC
DECLARE parameter_value2_3 = VC
SET parameter_value1 = parameter(1,0)
SET parameter_value2_1 = parameter(2,1)
SET parameter_value2_2 = parameter(2,2)
SET parameter_value2_3 = parameter(2,3)
SET parameter_value3_1 = parameter(3,1)
SET parameter_value3_2 = parameter(3,2)
; ...

PARAMETER2.summary: The Parameter2( ) function returns the parameter number for the $param_name. It is often used within the Parameter( ) function, which requires the parameter number. The Parameter2() function was introduced in version 8.7.0 of Discern Explorer .
PARAMETER2.example:
; ...

;determine the prompt number of the prompt named "gender"
set gender_num = parameter2($gender)

;check to see if multiple values were selected at the $gender prompt
set lcheck = substring(1,1,reflect(parameter(parameter2($gender),0)))

call echo(gender_num)
call echo(lcheck)


end
; ...

PARSER.summary: The PARSER( ) function allows you to build dynamic statements.

params.name: statement
params.description: A statement that is passed into a Discern Explorer command. Before Discern Explorer version 8.7.2 the statement was limited to a maximum of 32,000 characters. Discern Explorer version 8.7.2 increased the maximum to 100,000 characters.

PARSER.example:
DROP PROGRAM TEST1 GO
CREATE PROGRAM TEST1
SET NAME1 = "TEST"
SET WHERE1 = 'P.NAME_FIRST_KEY = NAME1'
SET WHERE2 = 'P.NAME_LAST_KEY = "PERSON"'
SELECT	P.PERSON_ID
FROM	PERSON P
WHERE	PARSER(WHERE1) AND PARSER(WHERE2)
END
GO

PATSTRING.summary: The PATSTRING( ) function treats an expression as a pattern-matching literal string. For example, when qualifying on records that have a field equal to TEST*, the function finds all instances that start with the letters "TEST" followed by any combination of characters. This allows the index to be read when pattern matching in qualifications or conditionals.

params.name: expression
params.description: A value of any data type.

params.name: mode
params.description: If the optional mode argument is used, the pattern match is applied during the processing phase (dynamic patstring); otherwise, this is done during the semantic phase.

PATSTRING.table:
| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Converts the expression to a Discern Explorer pattern-matching string |
| 1 | Converts the expression to an RDBMS pattern-matching string |
| 2 | Converts the expression to a Discern Explorer pattern-matching string using escape ( "\" ) |
| 3 | Converts the expression to an RDBMS pattern-matching string using escape ( "\" ) |
PATSTRING.example:
CASE(STR_VAR)
	OF ( PATSTRING("TEST*",0)): CALL ECHO("STR_VAR begins with 'TEST' ")
	OF ( PATSTRING("NOTEST*",0)): CALL ECHO("STR_VAR begins with 'NOTEST' ")
ELSE  CALL ECHO("NOT FOUND")
ENDCASE

PAUSE.summary: The CALL PAUSE command causes a program to wait for the defined number of seconds. This slows the display so users can read messages or watch information placed on the screen before other CALL commands refreshes or clears it. CALL PAUSE should only be used in interactive back end Discern Explorer Screen Application programs. Using CALL PAUSE in programs that run through servers creates inefficient delays in the program.

params.name: Seconds
params.description: The number of seconds to pause the screen.

PERCENT.summary: By default, the PERCENT( ) function returns the value from the result set where 50 percent of the values come before the returned value. Use the PERCENTILE( ) function to specify a different percentage. PERCENT( ) is valid when used in the FOOT section of a report, or as a select expression with some restrictions.

params.name: expression
params.description: A numeric value.

params.name: percent_num
params.description: A numeric value representing the percentage.

PERCENT.example:
; ...
	COL 50 "75%"
	ROW +1
	COL 10 PERCENT(RES)	";L"
	COL 30 PERCENT(PERCENTILE(RES,25))	";L"
	COL 50 PERCENT(PERCENTILE(RES,75))	";L"
	ROW +1
WITH NOCOUNTER

PERCENTILE.summary: By default, the PERCENT( ) function returns the value from the result set, where 50 percent of the values come before the returned value. The PERCENTILE( ) function can be used to specify a different percentile. It is used primarily within the PERCENT( ) function. If it is used in another context, PERCENTILE( ) returns the first parameter.

params.name: expression
params.description: A numeric value.

params.name: percent_num
params.description: A numeric value representing the percentage.

PERCENTILE.example:
; ...
	ROW +1
	COL 10 PERCENT(C.RES)	";L"
	COL 30 PERCENT(PERCENTILE(C.RES,25))	";L"
	COL 50 PERCENT(PERCENTILE(C.RES,75))	";L"
	ROW +1
WITH NOCOUNTER

PERCENTILE_CONT.summary: The PERCENTILE_CONT( ) function returns a value or interpolated value that represents a percentile from an ordered set of numeric values. PERCENTILE_CONT( ) can be used in the select list as an OLAP expression using the OVER( ) clause if using Discern Explorer version 8.8.0 or higher and Oracle 10g or higher. Discern Explorer version 8.9.2 introduced support for the WITHIN GROUP clause.

params.name: percentile
params.description: A numeric value between 0.0 and 1.0.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest level metasymbol among constants, column names, variables, and so on.

params.name: exp_name
params.description: The name to use as the column heading and select expression of the value returned by the PERCENTILE_CONT( ) function.

PERCENTILE_CONT.example:
SELECT
    P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID
    , P.RESULT_VALUE_NUMERIC
    , R_PERCENTILE_CONT = PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) OVER(PARTITION BY P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID
                                 ORDER BY P.RESULT_VALUE_NUMERIC )
FROM
    PERFORM_RESULT   P
WHERE P.UPDT_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTLOOKBEHIND("3,D") AND CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE, CURTIME3)
        AND P.RESULT_VALUE_NUMERIC > 0.0
        AND P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID != 0.0
ORDER BY
    P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID
; ...

PERCENTILE_DISC.summary: The PERCENTILE_DISC( ) function returns the smallest value that is greater than or equal to the value of a percentile in an ordered set of numeric values. PERCENTILE_DISC( ) can be used in the select list as an OLAP expression using the OVER( ) clause if using Discern Explorer version 8.8.0 or higher and Oracle 10g or higher. Discern Explorer version 8.9.2 introduced support for the WITHIN GROUP clause.

params.name: percentile
params.description: A numeric value between 0.0 and 1.0.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest level metasymbol among constants, column names, variables, and so on.

params.name: exp_name
params.description: The name to use as the column heading and select expression of the value returned by the PERCENTILE_CONT( ) function.

PERCENTILE_DISC.example:
SELECT
    P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID
    , P.RESULT_VALUE_NUMERIC
    , R_PERCENTILE_DISC = PERCENTILE_DISC(0.5) OVER(PARTITION BY P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID
                                 ORDER BY P.RESULT_VALUE_NUMERIC )
FROM
    PERFORM_RESULT   P
WHERE P.UPDT_DT_TM BETWEEN CNVTLOOKBEHIND("3,D") AND CNVTDATETIME(CURDATE, CURTIME3)
        AND P.RESULT_VALUE_NUMERIC > 0.0
        AND P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID != 0.0
ORDER BY
    P.PERFORM_PERSONNEL_ID
; ...

PERCENT_RANK.summary: The PERCENT_RANK( ) function returns a normalized rank expressed as a decimal in the range of 0 to 1 inclusively of a value in a group of rows. It returns the rank minus one divided by the number of rows in the partition minus one. PERCENT_RANK( ) can be used in the select list as an OLAP expression using the OVER( ) clause if using Discern Explorer version 8.8.0 or higher and Oracle 10g or higher.

params.name: constant

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| 1 | First | mode:r, rec:r, buf:rw | Set to the first child node of the parent. |
| 2 | Next | mode:r, rec:r, buf:rw | Set to the next sibling node of the parent. |
| 3 | SetPar | mode:r, rec:r, buf:rw, dim:r | Set to the parent node for this child node. |

| 9 | SetTotDim | mode:r, rec:r, buf:rw, totdim:r | Set the total dimension (size) of the segment. |

   declare rbuf = c300       with protect

   declare RTMFirst = i1     with protect,constant(1) ;RecTraverse(<mode>,<rec>,<buf>)
   declare RTMNext = i1      with protect,constant(2) ;RecTraverse(<mode>,<rec>,<buf>)
   declare RTMSetPar = i1    with protect,constant(3) ;RecTraverse(<mode>,<rec>,<buf>,<dim>)
   declare RTMGetTotDim = i1 with protect,constant(4) ;RecTraverse(<mode>,<rec>,<buf>,<totdim>)
   declare RTMSetDim = i1    with protect,constant(5) ;RecTraverse(<mode>,<rec>,<buf>,<dim>)
   declare RTMGetName = i1   with protect,constant(6) ;RecTraverse(<mode>,<rec>,<buf>,<name>,<type>)

TDBEXECUTE.syntax: TDBEXECUTE(appid, taskid, reqid, request_from_type, request_from, reply_to_type, reply_to[,mode[[,flexmode]])
TDBEXECUTE.summary: The TDBEXECUTE( ) function traverses a Discern Explorer , JSON, or XML record and executes a TDB request. TDBEXECUTE( ) calls CrmBeginApp if it is executed from interactive Discern Explorer or appid is not 0, else it calls CrmGetAppHandle to retrieve an application handle. Calling CrmBeginApp updates the Application_Context table. TDBEXECUTE() returns 0 if successful and 1 if an error occurred.

params.name: appid
params.description: The application id.

params.name: taskid
params.description: The task id.

params.name: reqid
params.description: The request id.

params.name: request_from_type
params.description: "REC" | "JSON" | "XML"

params.name: request_from
params.description: The input record for type "REC" or the input buffer for type "JSON" or type "XML". The request_from must provide the information that is expected by the TDB request.

params.name: reply_to_type
params.description: "REC" | "JSON" | "XML"

params.name: reply_to
params.description: The output record for type "REC", or the output buffer for type "JSON" or "XML". The reply created by the execution of the TDB request is assigned to reply_to.

params.name: mode
params.description: Introduced in version 8.8.1 of Discern Explorer , it allows Modes 0 and 1. Discern Explorer version 8.12.1 added Modes 2, 3, 4, and 5.

params.name: flexmode
params.description: Introduced in Discern Explorer versions 8.14.0 and 9.02.0 .

TDBEXECUTE.table:
| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No persist and show errors. The default mode before Discern Explorer version 8.12.5. |
| 1 | No persist and suppresses errors for set of <reply_to> (warning3 trace can be used to show them). |
| 2 | Persist output record <reply_to> and show errors. |
| 3 | Persist output record <reply_to> and suppress errors. |
| 4 | Persistscript output record <reply_to> and show errors. |
| 5 | Persistscript output record <reply_to> and suppress errors. |
TDBEXECUTE.example:
; ...
   set requestin->qual[1]->person_id = 123456
   set requestin->qual[1]->birth_dt_tm = cnvtdatetime("01-jan-2010 08:30")
   set stat = tdbexecute(3055000,4801,3091001,"REC",requestin,"REC",ReplyOut)
   call echo(build("tdbexecute=",stat))
   call echorecord(requestin)
   call echorecord(replyout)

TRIM.summary: TRIM () returns a result of type String that is a specified text expression stripped of any leading, embedded, or trailing characters that are less than or equal to spaces. TRIM() is a varchar function.

params.name: text_expr
params.description: A text expression.

params.name: trim_option
params.description: An integer that determines which spaces are stripped from an expression. If omitted, Option 1 is used by default. The following options are valid

TRIM.table:
| Option | Description | Definition | Passed to RDBMS Query As |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Trim trailing characters that are less than or equal to a space (default). | Trim trailing char(0) and char(3) to char(32) | RTRIM(text_expr) |
| 2 | Trim leading characters that are less than or equal to a space. | Trim leading char(0) and char(3) to char(32) | LTRIM(text_expr) |
| 3 | Trim trailing and leading characters that are less than or equal to a space. | Trim leading and trailing char(0) and char(3) to char(32) | RTRIM(LTRIM(text_expr)) |
| 4 | Trim leading and embedded characters that are less than or equal to a space. | Trim leading and embedded char(0) to char(32) | Unsupported RDBMS command or command in error |
| 5 | Trim trailing spaces. | Trim trailing char(32) | RTRIM(text_expr) |
| 6 | Trim leading spaces. | Trim leading char(32) | RTRIM(text_expr) |
| 7 | Trim leading and trailing spaces. | Trim leading and trailing char(32) | RTRIM(text_expr) |

| 9 | Trim embedded characters that are less than or equal to a space but not leading spaces. | Trim embedded char(0) to char(32) | RTRIM(text_expr) |

TRIMBIND.summary: The TRIMBIND function can be used to optionally control the bind parameter string length and maximize binding in the shared pool cache since the RDBMS creates a new shared pool cache instance based on the length. This reduces the RDBMS bind mismatch due to varying string lengths.

params.name: expression
params.description: A character data type value.

TRIMBIND.table:
| Mode | Description |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Use small bind length to pad |
| 2 | Use medium bind length to pad |
| 3 | Use medium large bind length to pad |
| 4 | Use large bind length to pad |
| -length | Use absolute length for the bind length |
TRIMBIND.example:
set trace rdbdebug go
	set trace rdbbind go

	SELECT INTO "nl"
		r.description
	FROM request   r
	WHERE r.description = trimbind("ABC",-3)
	WITH nocounter
	GO
