UPDATE.syntax:
UPDATE [FROM/INTO table_name [alias] {,table_name [alias]}]
    SET update_expression = expression {,update_expression = expression}
    [PLAN range [WHERE qualification]
    {join_operator range [WHERE qualification]}]
    [WHERE qualification]
    WITH update_option GO
UPDATE.summary: The UPDATE command updates existing rows in a table. Only authorized Oracle personnel should use the UPDATE command on Oracle production tables. Your RDBMS sign-on controls which RDBMS tables you can update. To UPDATE rows on a non-RDBMS table, you must issue a DEFINE command with the MODIFY option to allow updates to the file; otherwise, the file is opened as read-only.

params.name: alias
params.description: The abbreviated name of a table to be used in place of the table name when referencing the table in any part of the DELETE, INSERT, RANGE, SELECT, and UPDATE commands.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest-level metasymbol among constants, field names, variables, and so on. The following expressions are valid

params.name: join_operator
params.description: In the context of a PLAN clause, defines whether Discern Explorer performs a linear read between tables (JOIN), or performs a union of two tables (ORJOIN). Valid values are JOIN and ORJOIN.

params.name: qualification
params.description: A condition that limits the number of records to be updated. Qualifications can include IF, IN, and CASE statements and can be combined using the qualifiers AND, OR, NOT, and BETWEEN. Relational operators are used to define the condition.

params.name: table_name
params.description: The name of the table from the Discern Explorer Data Dictionary that you want to update, delete, or read.

params.name: update_expression
params.description: The name of the table and field, as well as any substring of a field, to be searched for and updated in the records of a table. The syntax for valid update expressions is shown below.

params.name: update_option
params.description: Valid actions you can take when issuing an UPDATE command. Valid UPDATE options are described below.

UPDATE.example:
DEFINE TABLE_X IS "TABLE_X.DAT" WITH MODIFY

UPDATE INTO TABLE_X X
SET X.NAME="MURCER, BOBBY",
    X.TYPE="I"
WHERE X.NAME="MUCER, BOBBY"

VALIDATE.summary: The VALIDATE( ) function verifies whether a variable or record structure, or record structure item exists. This function can accept one or two arguments. If only one argument is used, the VALIDATE( ) function returns 1 if the expression exists, or 0 if the expression does not exist. When two arguments are used, if the first expression exists, the value of the first expression is returned; otherwise, the value of the second expression is returned.

params.name: expression1
params.description: Any variable or record structure item. Discern Explorer versions 8.14.3, 9.02.3, and higher allow a function for expression1.

params.name: expression2
params.description: Any variable, record structure item, or literal value.

VALIDATE.example:
; ...
DETAIL
     COL 0   "REC1->QUAL[1]: "
     X = VALIDATE(REC1->QUAL[1].SUB_ITEM,"N")
     COL+1   X
     ROW+2
     COL 0   "REC2->QUAL[1]: "
     Y = VALIDATE(REC2->QUAL[1].SUB_ITEM,"N")
     COL+1   Y
     ROW+2
     COL 0   "VAR_X: "
     A = VALIDATE(VAR_X,"N")
     COL+1   A
; ...

VALUE.summary: Before a command is executed, the VALUE( ) function converts a variable or expression to a literal value before it is substituted for a parameter. By default, variables are passed by the actual name, not the value represented by the variable name. The VALUE( ) function overrides the default and passes the value of the variable or expression.

params.name: expression
params.description: A value of any data type.

VARIANCE.summary: The VARIANCE ( ) function returns the variance of an expression that is an integer or real number, across the specified break. VARIANCE( ) can be used in the FOOT REPORT or FOOT group_expression sections of a Discern Explorer Select command.

params.name: expression
params.description: An expression is the highest level metasymbol among constants, column names, variables, and so on. A numeric expression must be used to calculate the variance.

params.name: exp_name
params.description: The name to use as the column heading and select expression of the value returned by the VARIANCE( ) function.

params.name: int
params.description: An integer value.

VARIANCE.example:

	ROW +1
FOOT C.ENCNTR_ID
	COL 10 "Variance:"
	COL +1 VARIANCE(TEMP_REAL) "###.##"
	ROW +1
WITH NOCOUNTER, SEPARATOR=" ", FORMAT
